skills.name: afk
skills.description: Continue already-authorized work while the user is away from the keyboard, sleeping, eating, commuting, or otherwise unavailable. Use when the user says they are leaving and wants Codex to keep working, monitor tasks, finish, babysit, or perform cleanup without further interaction. Advance independent wrap-up while leaving unrelated suspended work untouched; resolve only blocking in-scope choices from established preferences, project instructions, code evidence, and the simplest-correct default.

skills.name: ask-matt
skills.description: Choose the smallest useful skill or workflow for the current situation.

skills.name: capability-pruning
skills.description: Prune a codebase by capability — inventory every capability, give each an evidence card, and let the owner decide removals item by item. Use when simplifying or slimming a project, hunting for unused features or dead mechanisms, or before claiming that something is unused, never used, or safe to delete.

skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Review a branch, PR, or work-in-progress diff against a fixed base for correctness, requirements, and consequential coding standards. Use one combined reviewer by default and add reviewers only for distinct material risks.

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.description: Structured feedback-loop diagnosis for exceptionally difficult, stubborn, recurring, high-regression-risk, or previously misfixed bugs. Ordinary, localized, first-pass bugs stay outside this skill.

skills.name: domain-modeling
skills.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR.

skills.name: e2e-first-testing
skills.description: Test strategy for a repository — which tests to write, keep, or delete. Use when adding tests for a change or a bug fix, designing fakes, mocks or test doubles, reviewing a diff that adds or edits tests, deciding whether a regression test is warranted, or pruning a slow or brittle test suite.

skills.name: false-green
skills.description: Run a comprehensive false-green audit of tests and their verification gates.

skills.name: grill-me
skills.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

skills.name: grill-with-docs
skills.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

skills.name: grilling
skills.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea, from its design intent through an implementable shape. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

skills.name: handoff
skills.description: Curate a compact handoff when the user requests one, ownership moves, or substantial remaining work needs a fresh context. Preserve decisions, source pointers, exact state, and valid evidence.

skills.name: implement
skills.description: Implement agreed work with timely verification and review.

skills.name: implement-spec
skills.description: Implement the result of /to-spec and /to-tickets in code.

skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture
skills.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

skills.name: llm-agent-surface
skills.description: Design rules for what an LLM sees inside an agent framework — tool schemas, rejection messages, prompts — and for where the framework stops and the model decides. Use when building or changing an LLM agent, adding a tool or a schema field, writing a rejection or validation message, fixing a wrong model decision, or adding validation, retries or guards around model output.

skills.name: minimal-design-gate
skills.description: A gate against over-design, applied before and after a change. Use when proposing a design or a fix, writing a brief for another agent, reviewing a diff or an agent's delivery, or when a change adds fields, options, abstractions, fallbacks, compatibility paths or dependencies.

skills.name: pr
skills.description: Use when writing a PR body.

skills.name: prototype
skills.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

skills.name: reduce-complexity
skills.description: Reduce accidental complexity in ideas, plans, ADRs, and specifications before implementation. Use for a spec audit, subtraction audit, complexity budget, simpler architecture, or over-engineering review at the product and architecture surface; use simplify-code for implementation changes.

skills.name: repo-audit-loop
skills.description: Audit a whole repository, or a batch of finished work, until a round finds nothing — coverage ledger over every tracked file, orthogonal lenses, spec–code sync, every public entry actually run, and a defect ledger cleared as you go. Use when asked to audit, review or health-check a project, when closing out a batch of changes, before a release or handover, or when checking that specs and code still agree.

skills.name: research
skills.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and deliver findings in Markdown by default, using HTML only for an explicitly requested polished human-facing report. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

skills.name: retro
skills.description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

skills.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
skills.description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

skills.name: shared-skills-manager
skills.description: Install, update, inspect, or schedule updates for the public starrybamboo/agent-skills catalog. Invoke explicitly with setup, update, status, pause, resume, disable, or schedule.

skills.name: simplify-code
skills.description: Simplify existing implementation code, tests, modules, state, or operational machinery without changing approved behavior, architecture, or failure policy. Use when the user asks to simplify code, remove over-engineering, clean up a reviewed diff, or when an authorized implementation workflow reaches its final simplification pass.

skills.name: site-annotated-gates
skills.description: Enforce architectural and code-shape rules with static gates whose exceptions are annotated at the code site. Use when adding a lint or CI check for an architectural constraint, when a test is about to lock code structure, when an allowlist or exemption list keeps growing, or when a rule needs justified exceptions.

skills.name: structural-fix
skills.description: How to fix a defect so its whole class disappears, not just the reported instance. Use when fixing a bug, writing a fix brief for another agent, reviewing someone's fix, or when a fix is tempting to write as a guard, special case, retry cap or fallback.

skills.name: tdd
skills.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

skills.name: teach
skills.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

skills.name: to-questionnaire
skills.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

skills.name: to-spec
skills.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

skills.name: to-tickets
skills.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).

skills.name: triage
skills.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

skills.name: unslop
skills.description: Remove stock AI phrasing, empty abstraction, promotional filler, rigid structure, and punctuation tells from natural-language prose while preserving its meaning and intended tone. Use whenever drafting, rewriting, polishing, or reviewing user-facing prose; skip code, exact quotations, and wording that must remain unchanged.

skills.name: wait-what
skills.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.

skills.name: wayfinder
skills.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

skills.name: wizard
skills.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

skills.name: writing-for-agents
skills.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
